notes: CONFORMS (2026-11-16, kb/Work PB5886 with its review round 2): §1989:A.2.2 AR4 "An arithmetic expression which will always result in an integer value must be specified" (cite.py OK). The screen FAILS CLOSED at --std 85 as at every edition (IntegerViolation's expression arm, NotAlwaysIntegral) and decides by the types of the terms and the values of the literals: an integer term (ProvablyIntegral: an integer literal or exact literal fold, an integer data item, a function of the integer type its definition's table gives for the argument types, +, -, * and unary - over integer terms, an integer term to an exponent that cannot be negative, the literal 1 to any integer exponent, IsIntegerPower), a quotient by a literal whose reciprocal terminates read as the product by that reciprocal, and a sum of items under literal factors whose net coefficient the item's scale makes whole (CollectAdditive). Everything else is refused with COBOL1627: FACTORIAL (FUNCTION ORD (A) / 2), FACTORIAL (FUNCTION MOD (N 3) * 0.5), FACTORIAL (FUNCTION INTEGER (N) / FUNCTION INTEGER (M)), MOD (I / I + 65, 7), FACTORIAL (S2 - FUNCTION MAX (S2)) over a scaled S2 and MOD (1024 ** K, 7) (witnesses pb5886-*), with the earlier refusals pb5208-*, pb5832-*; a form that is an integer only by an identity between numeric function terms is refused as recorded debt (kb/Work PB5889, pb5889-identity-difference). The admitted shapes are pinned by pb5886_integer_term_shapes, pb5832_scaled_integral_shapes, pb5345_power_failopen_shapes and the shape table of IntrinsicTypeSixPowerShapesDriftTests. 1985 has no EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION, so this screen is the rule's whole enforcement. The ALL subscript half holds (ORD-MAX and ORD-MIN over TC (ALL, ALL), TC (ALL, 2), an ODO range; witness 1989-AR-A_2_2-4). retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs#ItemWitness (kb/Work PB5886: the type 6 screen fails closed; the witness arms are gone and NotAlwaysIntegral / CollectAdditive / ProvablyIntegral show integrality instead) retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs#PowerWitness (kb/Work PB5886: the type 6 screen fails closed; the witness arms are gone and NotAlwaysIntegral / CollectAdditive / ProvablyIntegral show integrality instead) retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs#WitnessOf (kb/Work PB5886: the type 6 screen fails closed; the witness arms are gone and NotAlwaysIntegral / CollectAdditive / ProvablyIntegral show integrality instead)

next.reason: §1989:A.2.2 AR4, as amended in place by X3.23b-1993: out-of-range arguments - 'then the result of such a reference is undefined' (printed: 'the returned value for the function is undefined'), and an ALL subscript yielding no argument - 'otherwise the result of the reference to the function-identifier is undefined' (printed: 'otherwise the returned value is undefined'). The amendment changed what is undefined (the reference, not only the returned value); it changed no accepted program. §2023:15.3 AR14 keeps the ALL-subscript expansion word for word, including 'otherwise the result of the reference to the function-identifier is undefined', and §2023:8.4.2.3.4 GR1 restates it ('If ALL is specified, the subscript is all of the possible values of a subscript for the associated table'). But for out-of-range arguments 2023 replaces 'undefined' with 'the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist' and, when checking is not enabled, 'the implementor defines the result of the function reference': undefined made an exception condition and implementor-defined. 2023 also adds a case: 'If the subscript ALL is specified for a dynamic-capacity table, the range of values of the subscript is from 1 to the current capacity of the table'. The integer argument type is unchanged in substance: §2023:15.3 AR6 'An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified' against 1989 'An arithmetic expression which will always result in an integer value must be specified' (an integer data item is such an expression).
